headline: HONEY BADGER SILVER DRILLS 1,535 G/T AgEq OVER 4.38m AT SUNRISE LAKE — First 2026 Holes Hit; New Zone Found 400m North of Historic Resource in NWT
snippet: Honey Badger Silver (TSX-V: TUF) reported its first 2026 drill results at the Sunrise Lake silver-zinc project in the Northwest Territories, returning 1,535 g/t silver-equivalent over 4.38 metres and a second interval of 1,154 g/t AgEq over 7.30 metres — exceptionally high grades that rank among the best silver drill intercepts of any TSX-V program this year. A further highlight is new pyrite-galena mineralisation discovered approximately 400 metres north of the historic resource boundary, extending the system in a direction not previously tested and providing fresh targets for follow-up drilling beyond the known deposit.

headline: QMINES DRILLS 46.8m @ 2.29% Cu AND 1.03 G/T Au BENEATH OLD MT CHALMERS PIT — High-Grade Copper-Gold Extends at Depth in Queensland
snippet: QMines (ASX: QML) drilled 46.8 metres at 2.29% copper and 1.03 g/t gold below the floor of the old Mt Chalmers pit in Queensland, confirming that high-grade copper-gold mineralisation extends well beneath the historic open-pit workings and remains open at depth. Mt Chalmers was an operating copper mine, so an intercept of this grade and width beneath the existing pit places the project among the more attractive copper-gold development candidates in Queensland — a jurisdiction with established permitting frameworks and regional processing infrastructure.

headline: CHALLENGER GOLD FIRST HOLES RETURN 57.7m @ 1.31 G/T AuEq AT HUALILÁN — Matches PFS Widths and Grades; Argentina Mine Study Model Fully Validated
snippet: Challenger Gold (ASX: CEL) reported that its first drill holes at the Hualilán project in Argentina returned 57.7 metres at 1.31 g/t gold-equivalent — matching the widths, shapes, and grades built into the company's pre-feasibility study resource model, providing direct validation of the geological assumptions underlying its mine development economics. For junior mining investors, an independent drill campaign that replicates rather than challenges a PFS model is the strongest possible signal ahead of construction financing, reducing the technical risk premium typically applied to Argentine development-stage assets.

headline: SATURN METALS DRILLS 9m @ 12.91 G/T Au EAST OF CURRENT PIT DESIGN AT APOLLO HILL — High-Grade Extension Opens New Zone in Western Australia
snippet: Saturn Metals (ASX: STN) returned 9 metres at 12.91 g/t gold from drilling at Apollo Hill in Western Australia, with the high-grade interval extending the deposit to the east, beyond the boundary of the current pit design. At 12.91 g/t, the grade significantly exceeds the resource average and suggests a structurally controlled high-grade corridor that could improve the project economics if confirmed by follow-up drilling.

headline: KAOKO METALS FIRST HOLE RETURNS 54m @ 1.03% Cu AND 29.2 G/T Ag AT DONKEY HILL — Namibia Copper Project Opens With Strong First Intercept
snippet: Kaoko Metals (ASX: KAO) reported that its first ever drill hole at the Donkey Hill copper project in Namibia returned 54 metres at 1.03% copper and 29.2 g/t silver — a strong opening result that also carries meaningful silver by-product credits. Namibia is a pro-mining jurisdiction with established infrastructure and direct export access; a first-hole copper result of this grade and width confirms the company successfully converted surface geochemistry and geological work into a drill-ready discovery.

headline: OSISKO METALS OUTLINES 7.4B LB UNDERGROUND COPPER AT GASPÉ — Grades Nearly TWICE the Open Pit Average; Eastern North America's Largest Undeveloped Cu Deposit Grows Again
snippet: Osisko Metals has outlined an underground copper resource of approximately 7.4 billion pounds at the Gaspé project in Québec, grading at nearly double the average copper grade of its already-defined open-pit measured and indicated resource of 10.8 billion pounds — adding a high-grade underground mining scenario to the existing large-tonnage open-pit option. The combined picture reinforces Gaspé's position as the largest undeveloped copper deposit in eastern North America and expands the range of development strategies available to the company and any potential acquirer.

headline: IMC RARE EARTHS POSTS FIRST H1 RESULTS AFTER NYSE AMERICAN IPO — Terbium and Yttrium Discoveries at Itarantim, Brazil; $18.7M Cash in Hand
snippet: IMC Rare Earths (NYSE American: IMC) reported its first half-year results since its July 2026 IPO that raised $23 million, disclosing $18.7 million in cash and announcing new terbium and yttrium discoveries at its Itarantim project in Bahia, Brazil — critical elements used in permanent magnets for electric motors and wind turbines. Despite the November rare earth sector selloff, the stock has held a 53% premium to its $5 IPO price at around $7.64, reflecting investor interest in a pure-play rare earth developer listed in the US at a time when Western governments are urgently seeking non-Chinese supply.

headline: CAMECO SURGES 7.4% AS NVIDIA'S HUANG SIGNALS MASSIVE AI CAPACITY EXPANSION — Uranium Stocks Rally on Nuclear Power Demand Thesis
snippet: Uranium stocks rallied on November 23 after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced a major AI capacity expansion that markets read as increasing nuclear power demand, with Cameco gaining 7.4% in New York despite analysts noting the move does not change uranium's fundamental supply-demand equation. For TSX-V uranium investors, the Cameco rally following tech news illustrates the AI-energy thesis that has periodically re-energised the uranium sector through 2026 — though the disconnect between stock price catalysts and underlying spot uranium supply-demand remains a risk for momentum chasers.

headline: NRC OPENS COMMENT PERIOD ON CROWNPOINT/CHURCH ROCK ISR URANIUM LICENSE — Dec. 21 Deadline; NM Attorney General Cleared to Intervene Against NuFuels Renewal
snippet: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission opened a public comment period through December 21 on its draft environmental assessment for NuFuels' license renewal at the Crownpoint in-situ recovery uranium project in McKinley County, New Mexico — a rare major uranium permitting milestone in a jurisdiction historically resistant to mining development. New Mexico's Attorney General has been cleared to intervene in the proceeding with contentions including a challenge to whether aquifer restoration is feasible, making Crownpoint one of the most closely watched uranium regulatory proceedings in the US for Laramide Resources investors.

headline: JUNIOR GOLD MINERS POST SECOND-HIGHEST QUARTERLY PROFIT EVER — GDXJ TRADES AT 4-YEAR VALUATION LOW Despite Record Earnings
snippet: Junior and mid-tier gold miners in the GDXJ top 25 posted their second-highest quarterly profit on record in Q2 2026, earning an implied $3,214 per ounce — yet the ETF is trading at its cheapest price-to-earnings ratio in 41 quarters, the most extreme earnings-valuation disconnect in the GDXJ's history with a 16x trailing P/E against second-highest-ever earnings. For self-directed investors evaluating entry timing in the November correction, the analysis frames the current dislocation as historically consistent with a major re-rating event once Fed rate expectations resolve, though analysts caution that the GDXJ was similarly 'cheap' for extended stretches of 2022 before the eventual recovery.

headline: PLATINUM GROUP METALS REPORTS FY2026 ANNUAL RESULTS — Waterberg PGM Project Advances Toward Development Decision as Implats Interest Dilutes
snippet: Platinum Group Metals (TSX: PTM, NYSE American: PLG) reported annual results for fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, with the company advancing the Waterberg palladium-platinum-gold project in South Africa toward a construction decision — the key development milestone investors are tracking after Implats ceased funding cash calls and began diluting its interest. Waterberg is one of the world's largest undeveloped PGM deposits, and progress on concentrate offtake agreements and construction financing will be the defining metrics for investors seeking PGM exposure as South African supply disruption risks re-emerge.

headline: GOLDEN DRAGON MINING HITS DEEPEST HIGH-GRADE GOLD YET AT COODARDY — 4m @ 7.84 G/T FROM 70m; Fresh Rock Zone Extends in Western Australia
snippet: Golden Dragon Mining (ASX: GDR) drilled 4 metres at 7.84 g/t gold from 70 metres depth at its Coodardy project in Western Australia — the company's deepest high-grade gold intersection in fresh rock yet, indicating the mineralised system extends to depth and is not limited to the oxide zone. A systematic fresh-rock gold discovery at 7.84 g/t at a small explorer suggests a geological profile capable of attracting larger company attention as follow-up drilling continues to extend the system.
